# Q3 whole-process synthetic fixture

Prepared only. Default tests read JSON/text and hashes; they do not import or execute any .mjs. The public extension command `/whole-process-probe <case-id>` is a future explicit entry, not a currently approved command. Merely importing the extension registers this command without file/network/process probes. No SDK namespace/prototype/private API is modified; the extension deliberately does direct Node IO and fixed own child spawn to exercise the complete process boundary rather than rely on tool approvals.

Each case needs a new private project/state/results tree and one new container. The image digest, exact current Node24/Pi candidate/extension source identity, non-root numeric UID/GID matching private bind ownership, native Pi public CLI arguments, container lifecycle and explicit authorization must be independently frozen first. `plan.json` is intentionally prepared-only with these fields null. Prepared-only permits the unresolved public CLI placeholder; a frozen declaration must instead provide a canonical /candidate/.../node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/dist/cli.js path with no dot/parent/control/backslash segments. This permits a package subdirectory without guessing current identity. Its frozen state label is not authority or evidence that that file/CLI actually runs. No Dockerfile/build/install/native runner or deployment change is supplied.

The candidate Docker scenario requires readonly rootfs, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, network none, pid limit32, memory512MiB, CPU1, no privileged/device/add-cap/host namespace/host docker.sock/host HOME mounts. Mount only readonly pinned candidate/Node/fixture and owner-compatible private project/state/results; use a bounded noexec/nosuid/nodev 16MiB tmpfs and an empty PATH. No arbitrary argv, child program, destination, project script or external URL is accepted. The only child source is child.mjs via fixed /node/bin/node, allow/deny arguments, timeout2s and output4096B; at most one child per case. Source helper loopback.mjs uses fixed container-local 127.0.0.1:35731 and outbound TEST-NET-1 192.0.2.1:35731 with 250ms timeout and 64B local sink budget. These are prepared assumptions, not verified Docker namespace/UID/cancellation facts.

Before each case, the future parent stages allowed.txt into the own project, auth.json into the own container state and a copy of host-sentinel.txt into a new own host-only directory outside **every** container mount. The sentinel text is deliberately public synthetic data, not a secret; having another copy in the readonly fixture does not expose or authorize the host-only path. The host-only file is never mounted at /outside-host/denied.txt. Future parent observes actual allowed-output bytes, unchanged inaccessible host-only sentinel outside **every** container mount, connection facts, child identity/count/status and complete container termination. Neither an extension-reported blocked status nor every operation failing suffices. A timeout/no target listener is not by itself network isolation proof: inspect actual Docker network-none namespace and independently observe no outbound connection/packet via an authorized parent-side observer before declaring network negative passed. Parent-side observation and later concrete argv freeze are required T039/Q3 work, not provided runtime evidence.

The container-native credential case intentionally expects readable `/state/pi-home/auth.json`, using only this own synthetic auth.json copy. A regular container cannot hide same-UID native Pi credentials from malicious extensions inside it. Do not copy host tokens/HOME/auth into the container, and do not claim this container blocks native account exfiltration. Network-none blocks legitimate external provider login/model traffic too; any later login/model/SSH network scenario needs its own narrower explicit policy and authorization. This package supplies no real accounts, SSH keys, tokens or live endpoint. Credential-in-container visibility is a limitation observation, not a negative isolation pass or an account qualification.

Q3 feasibility and real behavior, allowed/denied outcomes, image/platform versions, actual account/provider path and complete-process cleanup remain not-run. No unsupported conclusion or product/whole-Pi isolation claim follows from fixture/default tests. If this approach is later selected as supported, its real whole-process negative and allowed positive acceptance is mandatory and cannot replace the required managed-tool isolation gate.
